question.problem:
The inverse of the $2\times 2$ matrix $Q$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine ${Q}^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[Q\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \,4 & \,1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,-1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\phantom{a}} & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\phantom{a}} \\ 0 & 1 & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\phantom{a}} & \bbox[2pt,lightgray]{\phantom{a}}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We write down $Q$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $Q$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[Q\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & \,4 & \,1 & 0 \\ 0 & \,-1 & \,-1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-4){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -3 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The matrix ${Q}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{Q}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$
